text:
swans also die in spring

and there it floated

dead on a Sunday

turning sideways

in the current

and I went to the traffic circle

and made out

gods in cars,

dogs, women

turning,

and death

rushed down my throat

like a mouse,

and I heard the people coming

with their picnic baskets

and their laughter

and I felt guilty

for the swan

as if death

were something shameful

and I went away

like an idiot

and left them

my beautiful swan.

translation.title: Spring Swans
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the dead swan, public laughter, and the speaker's shame before ordinary death.
